clue.text: Yank after gold in China or another country

indicators.note: in tells us the gold-and-yank pair sits within the friend word

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate, so PAL

indicators.note: after places the yank word behind the gold word

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry
to yank is to tug

explanation.surface: A puzzle of national flags: something about gold, China and some other nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country the definition contrasts with, but it is china plate, rhyming slang for mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Portugal is a nation distinct from China, so it is simply another country.

clue.text: That man involved in porn, cast regularly to be thus?

indicators.note: involved in means the pronoun for that man sits within the letters picked out
regularly takes every second letter of porn and cast

parts.note: HE is the pronoun for that man

explanation.surface: A man caught up in a pornographic film, with the cast, is supposedly aroused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes even letters across both words, ignoring the comma; 'thus' points back at the porn scene the surface paints.
explanation.definitionFit: In a state of sexual arousal, an idiom first used of female animals in season.

clue.text: More than one X on side of Valentine present perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten, so more than one is TENS

indicators.note: side of takes an edge letter of Valentine, here its final one

explanation.surface: Kisses, marked as X, on the side of a Valentine card as a present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'X' looks like a kiss and 'present' like a gift, but X is ten and present is a grammatical form.
explanation.definitionFit: The present is one grammatical tense, alongside past and future, so it is an example.

clue.text: Bird displays shrewdness to bypass Latin test

indicators.note: to bypass means the shrewdness word goes around the Latin abbreviation

parts.note: guile is cunning shrewdness
the MOT is the annual UK roadworthiness test for vehicles

explanation.surface: A clever bird skips its Latin exam.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's yearly compulsory vehicle safety test.
explanation.definitionFit: Guillemots are black-and-white seabirds of the auk family nesting on cliff ledges.

clue.text: Experts in line revealing illness

indicators.note: in places the experts word inside the word for line

parts.note: a ley is a ley line, a supposed alignment of ancient sites
pros are professionals, experts

explanation.surface: Specialists studying a line of symptoms uncover a disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Leprosy is a chronic bacterial disease affecting skin and nerves, a specific illness.

clue.text: Meagrely-stocked supermarket with vacuous service

parts.note: Spar is a chain of convenience supermarkets in Britain and Europe

indicators.note: vacuous means emptied, so only the outer letters of service remain

explanation.surface: A poorly stocked supermarket where the service is empty and useless.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin and scanty: a meagrely-stocked shelf has few items scattered on it.

clue.text: Row around river for fish

indicators.note: around means the quarrel word surrounds the river abbreviation

parts.note: a spat is a quarrel or row

explanation.surface: A boat rowing round the river in search of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests oars, but it is a quarrel, rhyming with cow.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprat is a small herring-like sea fish, an example of fish.

clue.text: Doctor treated ulna inside one vehicle

indicators.note: inside places doctor and the reworked bone within the word for one

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

indicators.note: treated means handled or processed, so the letters of ulna are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor treats a broken arm bone inside an emergency vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges ULNA into ULAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambulance is an emergency vehicle carrying the sick and injured.

clue.text: Writer and vocalist covering No.1s of Annie Lennox

indicators.note: covering means the vocalist word wraps round the initials

parts.note: a vocalist is a singer

indicators.note: No.1s of takes the first letter of each of Annie and Lennox

explanation.surface: A writer and singer cover the hit records of pop star Annie Lennox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' and 'No.1s' look like cover versions of hits; they mean containment and initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: J D Salinger was the American novelist of The Catcher in the Rye.

clue.text: Ladies' fingers one's seen on seat, wiping off bit of eclair

indicators.note: wiping off removes a letter from the seat word

parts.note: behind is a word for the seat, the buttocks

indicators.note: bit of takes the first letter of eclair

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone eats a chocolate eclair on a seat, then wipes their fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: Ladies' fingers is another name for okra; bhindi is its Indian name.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra pods are known as ladies' fingers, and as bhindi in Indian cooking.

clue.text: Soldier retraced a launch's curve

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier

indicators.note: retraced means the a-and-launch pair is read backwards

parts.note: to lob is to launch something in a high arc

explanation.surface: A soldier follows back the arc of a launched missile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retraced' reverses A LOB into BOLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A parabola is the U-shaped curve traced by a thrown projectile.

clue.text: Crushing defeat settled later in court

indicators.note: in places the reworked letters inside the courting word

parts.note: to woo is to court

indicators.note: settled means put in order, so the letters of later are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crushing loss in a lawsuit, settled later in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settled' rearranges LATER into TERLO; 'court' is a verb, to woo, not a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon's final defeat lent its name to any decisive, crushing defeat.

clue.text: Fantasy books given as gift

parts.note: a tale is a story, a fantasy
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Fantasy novels handed over as a present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gift' looks like a present but means a natural ability.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift is a natural aptitude, a synonym for a special ability.

clue.text: Private American leaves coach with the German comedian

parts.note: a Tommy is a British private soldier

indicators.note: leaves means the American abbreviation departs from the coaching word

parts.note: to coach is to train
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A private soldier quits his coach and joins a German comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy Trinder was a British music-hall and television comedian of the mid-twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: A British stand-up comic famous for the catchphrase You lucky people.

clue.text: Excessively bristly growth coming over top of hedge causes complaint

parts.note: too means excessively

indicators.note: coming over means the moustache word encloses the letter taken from hedge

parts.note: tache is informal for moustache, a bristly growth

indicators.note: top of takes the first letter of hedge

explanation.surface: An overgrown, bristly hedge provokes a neighbour's complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an ailment, and toothache is a painful one.

clue.text: Pair of ungulates, the first shaved here in mid-Europe

indicators.note: the first shaved means the first animal loses its last letter

parts.note: a rhino and an eland, two hoofed mammals

explanation.surface: Two hoofed animals, one shorn, roam a central European region.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhineland is the region along the Rhine in western Germany, central Europe.

clue.text: Tie business upset by the foolish South American general

parts.note: to pin is to fasten or tie

indicators.note: upset turns the business abbreviation upside down in this down clue

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business

indicators.note: foolish suggests letters gone silly, so the is rearranged

explanation.surface: A tie business is upset by a foolish South American general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns CO into OC; 'foolish' rearranges THE into HET.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusto Pinochet was the Chilean army general who ran a military dictatorship.

clue.text: Mistress imparted fervent kiss to one's ear?

definitions.meaning: a lover outside a marriage, slang for an extramarital partner

definitions.text: imparted fervent kiss to one's ear?
definitions.meaning: read literally, nibbled at the side of someone's head

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a secret lover; literally, a nibble on the side of the head where the ear is.

clue.text: Adaptable market boosted by endless credit

indicators.note: boosted means lifted up, so in a down clue the market word reads upwards

parts.note: a sale is a market for goods

indicators.note: endless drops the final letter from the credit word

parts.note: tick is British informal for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A flexible market is propped up by unlimited credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boosted' reverses SALE into ELAS; 'endless' cuts TICK to TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic means flexible, able to stretch and adapt to circumstances.

clue.text: Swede perhaps rejected alcoholic drink in Andalusia's heartland

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the whole assembly reads upwards in this down clue
in places the drink inside the central letters of Andalusia

parts.note: the central three letters of the Spanish region's name, its heart
kir is a drink of white wine and blackcurrant liqueur

explanation.surface: A Swede refuses a drink in southern Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the whole assembly round, not just the drink. Ulrika Jonsson is a Swedish-born British TV presenter, hence a Swede.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulrika is a typical Swedish female forename, so a Swede, by example.

clue.text: English runner somewhat old to oust American

indicators.note: to oust means the old abbreviation replaces the American one

parts.note: rather means somewhat

explanation.surface: An English athlete, somewhat old, displaces an American rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' looks like an athlete but is a river; the Rother flows through Sussex and Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: A river runs, so in crosswords runner can mean river; the Rother is in England.

clue.text: Sporting event Ivy Leaguer backed?

indicators.note: backed means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a Yaler is a student of Yale, an Ivy League university

explanation.surface: An event an Ivy League student put money on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' looks like betting support but reverses YALER.
explanation.definitionFit: A relay is a team race where runners or swimmers take turns.

clue.text: Open Maurice's outside bar when converted, dividing beer

indicators.note: dividing means these letters split the beer word

parts.note: ale is a beer

indicators.note: outside takes the outer letters of Maurice
when converted means the bar word is turned round

parts.note: to ban is to bar

explanation.surface: Maurice's pub, outside, is opened after conversion into a beer hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when converted' reverses BAN into NAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Open here means receptive or willing, a synonym for amenable.

clue.text: Left old taxmen with annual returns, auditing accounts ending then?

indicators.note: returns means the pieces read back upwards

parts.note: IR is the Inland Revenue, the former UK tax authority
PA is per annum, yearly

explanation.surface: An accountant left the old taxmen with annual returns at year end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' looks like tax returns but reverses L IR PA.
explanation.definitionFit: The UK tax year ends on 5 April, so accounts are audited then.

clue.text: Smart lecturer dips into supplies for section of bookshop

parts.note: chic means smart or stylish

indicators.note: dips into means the lecturer abbreviation goes inside the supplies word

parts.note: a kit is a set of supplies or equipment

explanation.surface: A smart lecturer browses stock in a bookshop section.
explanation.definitionFit: Chick lit is a genre of light fiction for young women, shelved as a bookshop category.

clue.text: Commotion surrounds resistance shown by X Factor expert

indicators.note: surrounds means the commotion word goes round the resistance symbol

parts.note: ado is fuss or commotion
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
it is the indefinable quality of star appeal, the X factor

explanation.surface: A TV talent show judge stirs up a fuss about resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: The X Factor was a TV talent contest; here it means it, sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful and dexterous, a synonym for expert.

clue.text: Firm close to capacity making metal front

indicators.note: front means the metal word goes before the letter from capacity

parts.note: steel is a metal alloy

indicators.note: close to takes the last letter of capacity

explanation.surface: A firm working close to capacity makes a metal shop front.
explanation.definitionFit: Steely means hard and resolute, a synonym for firm.

clue.text: Rogue adversely starts to alter crops — part of GM industry?

parts.note: a cad is a rogue
ill means badly, adversely

indicators.note: starts to takes the first letters of alter and crops

explanation.surface: A rogue harms crops in the genetically modified farming industry.
explanation.walkthrough: GM looks like genetically modified but is General Motors, which makes the Cadillac.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadillac is a car brand owned by General Motors, so part of GM's motor industry.
